σάρκινος, -η, -ον
(σάρξ), [in LXX: 2Ch.32.8, Ezk.11.19; 36.26 (בָּשָׂר), Est.4.17, Pro.24.23 (Pro.29.27) * ;] 
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Rom.7.14, 1Co.3.1, 2Co.3.3, Heb.7.16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages…

σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;] 
flesh; 
__1. as in cl. generally, 
__(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: 1Co.15.39, 2Co.12.7, Gal.6.13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, 1Co.5.50 σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Luk.24.39 pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Rev.17.16; 19.18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, 2Ki.9.36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, Jas.5.3…

Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג), 
Serug: Luk.3.35.† 
(AS)

σαρόω, -ῶ 
late form of σαίρω, 
to sweep: with accusative, Luk.15.8 pass., Mat.12.44, Luk.11.25.†
(AS)

Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Gen.17.15), 
Sarah: Rom.4.19; 9.9, Heb.11.11, 1Pe.3.6.†
(AS)

Σάρων, -ωνος (accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן), 
the plain of Sharon: Act.9.35.†
(AS)

Satan , i. e. an adversary, enemy : name for the Devil , (New Testament) 
Hebr. word. (ML)

Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ
(so also Sir.21.30, but in 1Ki.11.14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό, 
Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): Mat.4.10; 12.26, Mrk.1.13; 3.23, 26; 4.15 Luk.10.18; 11.18; 13.16; 22.3, 31, Jhn.13.27, Act.5.3; 26.18, Rom.16.20, 1Co.5.5; 7.5, 2Co.2.11; 11.14, 1Th.2.18, 2Th.2.9, 1Ti.1.20; 5.15, Rev.2.9, 13; 2.24; 3.9; 12.9; 20.2, 7; addressed in person…

σάτον, -ου, τό
(Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Hag.2.17 (16)* ;] 
a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mat.13.33, Luk.13.21.†
(AS)
